features.title: Case Report: Severe Hepatotoxicity Induced by Acetaminophen Overdose
features.abstract: A 45-year-old male patient presented to the emergency department with severe jaundice, elevated liver enzymes (ALT 2500 U/L, AST 1800 U/L), and signs of acute liver failure following an intentional acetaminophen overdose of 15g taken 24 hours prior. The patient had no known liver disease. Physical examination revealed icteric sclera, hepatomegaly, and mild ascites. Laboratory findings showed elevated bilirubin (8.5 mg/dL), prolonged prothrombin time (INR 2.8), and thrombocytopenia. The patient was diagnosed with acetaminophen-induced acute liver injury and treated with N-acetylcysteine. Despite aggressive supportive care, the patient developed hepatic encephalopathy and required liver transplantation. This case highlights the severe hepatotoxicity that can occur with acetaminophen overdose and the importance of early recognition and treatment.
